title: ExecuteSQL with hard-coded name
description: Best-practice rule — an ExecuteSQL statement names a table occurrence or field as plain text in the SQL string instead of building the name from a field reference (GetFieldName or a name wrapper). The reference works today, but FileMaker does not track it: renaming the table occurrence or field breaks the query without any warning — ExecuteSQL then returns ?.
author: fm-lab rules

rule.rationale: Plain-text names are invisible to FileMaker's rename propagation. Every rename of a table occurrence or field is a silent breaking change for these queries.
rule.remediation: Build the identifiers from field references, e.g. GetValue ( Substitute ( GetFieldName ( TO::Field ) ; "::" ; ¶ ) ; 2 ) wrapped in Quote, or a custom function that does this — then FileMaker keeps the query in sync on rename.

meta.calibration: Built on CalculationSqlRefs (schema 1.42.0), rows with Resolution = name that resolve to an existing field or table occurrence. Since schema 1.42.0 these names also produce reads_field links, so the fields no longer count as unused — this rule is the place where the rename risk stays visible.
